Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: ABS is zero-marked; ERG suffix -lu/-ju is the only core case marker. Confirmed by McKelson Lesson 39-40.
curated_comment: Karajarri (kara1476, ISO gbd, Pama-Nyungan, Western Australia) is a consistently ergative language per McKelson (2004). ERG suffix -lu (after vowels) / -ju (after consonants) marks transitive A; ABS is zero-marked. This replaces all original '?' annotations, which were unresolved. Source is a 40-lesson pedagogical sketch grammar, limiting resolution of several features: GB409_6-7 (aspect not grammaticalized), GB409_11 (non-indicative mood data limited), GB409_12-13 (realis/irrealis absent), GB409_15, 16, 17, 19, 21 (insufficient data in source). Features with direct evidence: GB409_2=1, GB409_3=1 (personal pronouns take -lu as transitive subjects), GB409_4=1, GB409_5=1 (full NPs), GB409_8-10=1, GB409_14=1, GB409_18=1, GB409_20=1, GB409_22=0, GB409_23=0 (GEN=-kura), GB409_24=0 (COM=pari). Glottocode kara1476 is correct.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: 1SG takes ERG suffix -lu when transitive subject (ngajulu); bare ngaju for intransitive S.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: 2SG nyuntu takes -lu as transitive subject: nyuntulu kawa mayi walipikarti 'You take the tucker' (Lesson 5, p.6).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: 3rd person full NPs take -lu/-ju as transitive subjects: wakalalu jinkanu jurru 'the woman hit the snake' (Lesson 39, p.39). Demonstrative pronouns also take -lu in A role.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs take ERG suffix -lu (after vowels) / -ju (after consonants): wakalalu (woman-ERG), wilarrju (turtle-ERG). McKelson p.39-40 explicitly explains the rule.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: Aspect (perfective/imperfective) is not a grammaticalized binary morphological category in this grammar; tense distinctions (present/past/future) are present but not aspect. Category absent.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Same as GB409_6: perfective/imperfective aspect not grammaticalized. Category absent.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: Past tense examples in Lesson 39-40 show ERG -lu/-ju on transitive subjects (jinkanu = past hit).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: No tense-based conditioning of ERG marking documented; -lu/-ju applies across tenses.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: All declarative/indicative examples show ERG marking on transitive A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: Imperative forms do not show -lu/-ju on A, but this appears to be a structural property of 2nd-person commands (not a mood-based split). Insufficient data for other moods.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: Realis/irrealis distinction is not a grammatical category in this grammar. Category absent.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Realis/irrealis distinction absent. Category absent.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: All documented A arguments (woman, turtle, person) are agentive and take ERG -lu/-ju.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: No examples of non-agentive A in source; insufficient data.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No discussion of topicality conditioning in source; insufficient data.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: No discussion of topicality conditioning; insufficient data.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: All ERG-marked A arguments in examples are animate (woman, turtle, people).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: No examples of inanimate A in transitive clauses in this source.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: All ergative examples occur in main clauses; ERG -lu/-ju consistently applies.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Source does not present subordinate clauses; insufficient data.

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: McKelson (p.39) states: 'lu and ju indicate an object-affecting subject' — a simple categorical rule with no additional conditioning mentioned.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Genitive/possessive = -kura (Lesson 7, p.8: japulukura 'father's'). Entirely distinct from ERG -lu/-ju.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Comitative = pari 'with' (Lesson 14, p.15: warnku pari 'with money'). Entirely distinct from ERG -lu/-ju.
